title: Install on Linux (including Raspberry Pi)
subtitle: Download one file, run one setup command, and (optionally) get a menu entry. Works on regular PCs and on ARM boards like the Raspberry Pi.
in_this_chapter: The Linux install in a nutshell
Which file to download (x64 vs ARM)
If the app won't start - missing system libraries

callout.label: IN A NUTSHELL
callout.text: Download the Linux **.tar.gz** for your processor from the Releases page, expand it (double-click, or  tar -xzf <file> ), open a terminal in that folder, and run  bash install.sh  . Press **Enter** at each prompt. There's no "unknown publisher" warning on Linux - it just installs. On a Raspberry Pi, use the **arm64** file.

blocks.p: Pick by your processor. Not sure? Open a terminal and run  uname -m  : if it prints **x86_64** you want x64; if it prints **aarch64** you want arm64.

rows: A regular Intel/AMD PC or laptop
An ARM board (Raspberry Pi 4/5, other 64-bit ARM)

callout.label: OLD 32-BIT ARM
callout.text: If you're on an old 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS (uname -m shows **armv7l**, e.g. a Pi Zero or Pi 2), that's the separate **linux-arm** build. It can work, but we strongly recommend the 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS on a Pi 4 or Pi 5 and the **arm64** file - the app runs much better there.

blocks.p: Activation Planner runs on a Raspberry Pi running the 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS desktop - a genuinely handy field option in a Pi laptop/netbook build. Use the **linux-arm64** download. One extra note: to get **real** predictions (not sample data), the two helper engines must be built on the Pi itself (they're ARM programs). The **Helper Engines** chapter and the maintainer appendix cover that; the app installs and runs either way.

steps: Open **https://github.com/KE4CON/ActivationPlanner/releases** in your browser and download the correct **.tar.gz**.

Expand it. In your file manager you can usually right-click -> **Extract Here**. Or in a terminal:  cd ~/Downloads  then  tar -xzf ActivationPlanner-1.0.0-linux-x64.tar.gz  (use your actual file name).
This creates a folder such as **ActivationPlanner-linux-x64** containing the app and **install.sh**.
Open a terminal in that folder (in many file managers: right-click -> **Open Terminal Here**), or  cd  into it.
Answer the few prompts (below). That's it.

blocks.p: Press **Enter** to accept the default in brackets for anything you're unsure about.

blocks.h1: If the App Won't Start - Missing System Libraries

blocks.p: On a very minimal Linux install, the graphical toolkit may need a few common libraries that aren't present yet. If the app fails to open, install the usual desktop libraries:

bullets: **Debian / Ubuntu / Raspberry Pi OS:**  sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y libice6 libsm6 libfontconfig1 libx11-6
**Fedora:**  sudo dnf install -y libICE libSM fontconfig libX11

blocks.p: Most desktop systems already have these, so you likely won't need this step.

rows: Run  uname -m . x86_64 -> the x64 file; aarch64 -> the arm64 file. Re-download the matching one.
